question.prompt: Let \(Z\) be a \(6\)-digit positive integer, such as \(247247,\) whose first three digits are the same as its last three digits taken in the same order. Which of the following numbers must be a factor of \(Z?\)

solutions.explanation:
The repeated block suggests treating its three digits as one number. Let \(n\) be that three-digit integer, so \(100\leq n\leq999\). In \(Z\), the first copy of the block has been shifted three places to the left, making its value \(1000n\). The last copy contributes \(n\). Therefore
\[
Z=1000n+n=1001n.
\]
Since \(1001=11\times91\), we have
\[
Z=11(91n).
\]
The quantity \(91n\) is an integer, so every allowed \(Z\) is a multiple of \(11\). The answer is \(\boxed{11}\), choice \(\text{A}\).
solutions.title: Use the repeated three-digit block
